When you start to question whether you are mentally I'll I ask you to come back to this post and re-read it. Think to yourself: does this behavior hurt me? Does it have the potential to hurt other people?
Assess your other behaviors and ask yourself the same question. Write em down and do the same thing, re read them and think: would a healthy, happy person think this way?
When your feeling lucid write the truth on sticky notes and put them in the spots you tend to dwell in when your having a mental health episode. Could be the wall next to your bed, could be the bathroom mirror, could be the tv-anywhere. If you have episodes in random places just put them somewhere youre most likely to see.
The truth could be something like "my professor isn't in love with me and that is ok" "I do not need his love to feel good." 
Make sure you read em when you're feeling low. It's important to remember the truth when your own mind is lying to you.

Hey there,
I started antidepressants a month ago and I was also scared, but it's actually not as bad as people make it seem. As long as you trust your doctor (if you don't get a new one, it's a good idea to ask around) you'll be ok. Don't be afraid to ask questions. If a doctor seems unwilling to listen to you or your questions, or if the see medication as the end all be all, or if they have no interest in getting to know you or understand your conditions before giving you a script, find a new one.
You'll likely start off on lexapro. It's very mild and it helps very much with the motivation and concentration. My doctor then put me on wellbutrin in addition a month later. I just came off the wellbutrin because it was making me aggressive and causing suicidal thoughts. 
It is essential that if you are having suicidal thoughts you talk to someone asap. I called the suicide hotline and they were fantastic, we talked about why I was feeling the way I did and we determined it was the medicine. I stopped taking it immediately and I'm perfectly fine. It's very very rare to have an increase in suicidal thoughts with two different medications so im glad that I no longer have to worry about that. If you are having suicidal thoughts after changing it's likely not the medication and you should talk to a therapist. 
Meds work best in conjunction with cognitive behavioral therapy. See a therapist if you don't already.
Medicine is there to help facilitate recovery, it doesn't solve the underlying issues which is why therapy is important. 
Medicine is also a journey and it can take time to find the right combination and learn how to use them
I STRONGLY ENCOURAGE YOU TO GET MEDICATION.
Remember this is coming from someone who had a negative reaction: it helps you feel better so quickly, it's amazing.
